boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Blair's Landing record (April 12-13, 1864) in the Red River Campaign [March-April 1864]. The fleet's ascent to Loggy Bayou, Liddell's fire from the east bank and the passage to Grand Ecore on April 14-15 are context; the April 13 firing at Bouledeau Point and Campti lies within the frozen interval but is recorded separately. Campaign-wide marches, returns, river operations and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Provisional division, XVII Army Corps, Army transports, and U.S. Navy Mississippi Squadron [US] and Green's Cavalry Division [CS]; the live field reads zero. Irwin and Taylor identify Green's force as Woods's and Gould's regiments and Parsons's brigade, with four batteries named by Irwin. Irwin says six gunboats convoyed twenty transports bearing Kilby Smith's division; Taylor's report says the fleet was about thirty vessels, only five carrying troops.
claims.rationale: Unit identifications and vessel counts that differ; no personnel count for either side. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

Taylor says Liddell engaged the fleet from the east bank on the 11th-13th. The frozen commanders are Brigadier General Tom Green, Brigadier General Thomas Kilby Smith and Rear Admiral David D. Porter; the live page lists Green and Thomas Smith, both as Brigadier General.
claims.rationale: Command roles from an interested report, a history and a summary; the listed commanders do not receive automatic sole credit, and no rank is adopted.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union victory and the live result Union Victory. Irwin says Kilby Smith and Porter drove off the attackers by sunset without great loss; Taylor says the loss on the crowded transports was terrible and that the whole fleet would have been captured but for Green's death; NPS says the Confederates withdrew and most transports continued downriver.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 207 total (US 7; CS 200); the live field reads 117 (US 60; CS 57). Irwin says Kilby Smith's division lost 19 above Grand Ecore, a figure covering the whole voyage, and that Porter mentions only one; Green was among the Confederate killed. Taylor calls the loss on the transports terrible and says several raised the white flag.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Irwin's 19 covers the voyage above Grand Ecore, not only April 12-13.

open_questions: T. Kilby Smith's and his subordinates' reports (Nos. 56-59), Hinkle's report (No. 64), Liddell's report (No. 105), Porter's and the other naval reports (Annual Report of the Secretary of the Navy, 1864, not in this volume) and any report for Green's command remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892) is a retrospective history by the former assistant adjutant-general of the corps and of Banks's Department of the Gulf, an interested Union account; it cites the Official Records and gives Taylor's and Kirby Smith's figures, so it is not independent of them. Taylor's April 18, 1864 report, his March 13-14 letters printed as its inclosures, his April 24-May 19 dispatches and his April 11 general order are one family of interested Confederate accounts. Official Records Series I, Volume XXXIV, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
